coverage.evidence: No secret is introduced or exposed. The changed file passes only GH_TOKEN, GitHub's own ephemeral job token, through env; it reads nothing else. Across both workflows the only project secret is secrets.FORBIDDEN_TERMS, unchanged here, and the guard that reads it prints positions rather than matches, deliberately, since the terms cannot live in the repository. gitleaks runs over full history on every pull request.

Everything the pipeline fetches travels over TLS: actions from GitHub, packages from https://registry.npmjs.org as pinned in package-lock.json. Nothing in this change adds an endpoint, and the product itself calls nothing - docs/02-architecture.md's Outside services section records none in the built app.

coverage.reason: No TLS configuration exists to review. The product is a static bundle that has not been deployed, and TLS is terminated by whichever CDN serves it; there is no server, load balancer or ingress in this project to set a cipher suite on. It becomes reviewable when hosting is chosen, issue #113.

coverage.evidence: The one secret, FORBIDDEN_TERMS, is a GitHub Actions repository secret, replaceable in the repository settings in seconds with no code change, since the workflow reads it by name only. GH_TOKEN is minted per job by GitHub and expires with the job, so it cannot be replaced because it never persists. Nothing in this change holds a long-lived credential.

The changed workflow declares least privilege explicitly: permissions contents: read and checks: read, and its checkout sets persist-credentials: false so the job's token is not left in the git config for later steps. pr-checks.yml declares contents: read. Neither grants write to anything. The checks: read permission is what next.17's CI reading needs and is the narrowest grant that serves it.

Nothing is made public by this change and nothing is exposed that was not. The repository is public deliberately, under PolyForm Noncommercial, and that is recorded in CONTEXT.md's repo rules. There is no network service to leave open: the product is a static bundle with no server, and the blob store ADR-013 designs does not exist yet.

Changes reach main only through a pull request with four checks green, and the project adds a gate of its own on top: npm run ci:premerge <pr> must print ALLOWED, which refuses a draft, a non-open pull request and any check that is not a pass, whatever the base branch. That last part matters here because branch protection is still off, issue #112, and it only ever guards main anyway. This change makes the Peer AI gate skip drafts, which does not weaken that: ci:premerge treats a skipped check as not passed, by the rule written in CLAUDE.md, and it refuses drafts outright.

coverage.reason: There is one environment, production, and no deployment yet. docs/02-architecture.md's Where it runs section records it: no staging, no per-environment build, and no environment variable the app reads at runtime. There is nothing to keep apart.

coverage.evidence: Real data cannot reach development or test, and this is enforced rather than intended. Every figure in fixtures, tests, screenshots and examples comes from docs/seed-data.md and is invented, which is repo rule 2, and the owner's own figures live only in their browser's IndexedDB. The repo-rules job in pr-checks.yml runs on every pull request. Nothing in this change touches data.

coverage.reason: There is no production to have access to: no server, no database, no hosting account in use yet. The question returns when hosting is chosen, #113, and ADR-013 shrinks it, since the only thing an operator could reach is a store of ciphertext it cannot read.

OPS-04 applies from production, and there is no staging environment because there is no production environment to mirror. Recorded as a deliberate absence in docs/02-architecture.md rather than an oversight.

Nothing server-side holds data to back up. The owner's data lives on their device, and its backup is the export file: a complete snapshot as JSON the owner holds, with a nudge when there are unexported changes, D12. That is the product's answer to durability and it is already built; it is not infrastructure.

No restore path or redundancy exists to test, for the same reason as OPS-05, and no uptime target has ever been recorded for this project - stated as not recorded in docs/02-architecture.md rather than assumed. Import is the restore path and it is tested: export then import round-trip, M3, in the core suite.

summary: Pass. The change is one workflow file gaining a draft condition and a version bump, and it moves nothing about privilege, secrets or exposure: permissions stay contents: read and checks: read, persist-credentials stays false, and the only secret is a repository secret read by name. Seven of thirteen rules are not applicable because there is no server, no second environment and nothing deployed, each with its reason.
